headline: Argentine Peso Depreciates to 1,600 per Dollar as Sovereign Risk Climbs
summary: Argentina's official retail dollar rate reached 1,600 pesos while financial exchange rates advanced, driven by global dollar strength, Brazilian real weakness, and a 150 percent surge in country risk over four months.
why: Argentina faces high structural inflation and thin foreign exchange reserves. Rapid currency depreciation and rising country risk spreads elevate international borrowing costs and strain national credit availability.

impacts.name: Argentine Peso
impacts.why: Local economic uncertainty and external currency pressures drove the peso to lower levels.
impacts.baseline_rule: first recorded price at or after created_at (15-minute price recorder); end = first price at least 24 h later, within 48 h

why_moved: External dollar strength and rising local political and fiscal uncertainty pushed Argentina's country risk higher and weakened the peso.
